title: Change a user’s password
purpose: Replace the selected user’s password as an administrator.

sections.title: Access and identity
paragraphs: The administration site requires an active account with Staff status. User and group pages additionally require Superuser status; a laboratory admin role alone or individual model permissions do not open them. These technical flags do not themselves confer operational roles or report-release authority.

This form identifies the target username and operates on that user, not necessarily the signed-in administrator. It requires user-change permission under the project’s superuser-only account administration.

items.label: Password-based authentication
items.description: Shown only when the target already has a usable password. Enabled is initially selected; Disabled removes usable password authentication and loses the old password. An account with an unusable password has no selector here and is being enabled.

items.label: Password / Password confirmation
items.description: Required matching replacement when enabling or keeping Enabled. Minimum eight characters and configured similarity/common/numeric-only validation apply. Password fields are not required when disabling.

items.label: Change password
items.description: Shown for a currently usable password; applies the enabled replacement after validation and returns to the target’s change form.

items.label: Disable password-based authentication
items.description: Shown for a currently usable password; choose Disabled and submit this action to invalidate its password. This does not provision another login method or remove MFA.

items.label: Enable password-based authentication
items.description: Shown for a currently unusable password; validates and saves the replacement.

items.label: Breadcrumbs
items.description: Return to the target user, Users list, module or administration home without changing the password.

sections.title: Recorded effect
paragraphs: A successful change, enable or disable operation records an attributed account.password_changed audit event and Django administration log entry without secret values. If changing your own password, Django updates this session’s authentication hash to preserve it. Laboratory roles, client link and release permissions do not change. No user invitation or password notification email is sent by this maintenance form.
